mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy easing supports risk asset performance.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% within the past month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns as recession risks increase and corporate earnings growth decelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) over the past 2 months indicates robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns as corporate earnings growth accelerates from strong consumer and industrial activity.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both rise > 0.5% in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where both HOUST and INDPRO have risen by at least 0.5% over the prior 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes where CPIAUCSL exceeds 195.0 and FEDFUNDS is above 4.0%, the Federal Reserve's tightening cycle reduces liquidity and increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 195.0 and FEDFUNDS > 4.0.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past 2 months signals strong consumer demand for residential real estate, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns as economic activity expansion supports corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances where HOUST has increased by at least 0.5% over the prior 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll growth rate below 0.1% indicates a slowing labor market, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns as weak hiring conditions reduce consumer spending and corporate revenue growth prospects.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS growth is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (RSAFS) over the past 2 months reflects robust economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns as strong supply chains and consumer demand accelerate corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and RSAFS both rise > 0.3% in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where both INDPRO and RSAFS have risen by at least 0.3% over the prior 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a rising CPIAUCSL coupled with stable FEDFUNDS signals the end of monetary easing, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns as the market prices in the transition to tightening cycles.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS change < 0.1%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL has risen by at least 0.5% and FEDFUNDS change is below 0.1%.
